note: Sources call it a Bronze Age ring cairn (period word only); no year, century or millennium is given.

No readable page prints a point for the Campu di Bonu cists; the stored point equals the centre of the commune of Bisinchi.

The enclosure is unexcavated; Wikipedia says only that it may have been an Iron Age hill fort, a period word with no year, century or millennium, and its general background on hill forts is a range for a whole class. No source gives a start year for this site.

No source prints a point for the Shaki Govurqala described by the English article (5th-14th-century walled settlement); the Baş Kəldək Gavur qalası (41.2092, 47.3664 on az.wikipedia) is described as a 6th-century Albanian temple and is not shown to be the same monument.

The only description is 'populated place' and 'walled defense stand with round and square towers'; no source names a canonical type word (fortification, fort, settlement) for this Govurqala, and the monument is not shown to be the Baş Kəldək Gavur qalası.

No source I could read prints a point for the al-Diwan chamber itself. The points on offer (English Wikipedia, Danish Wikipedia, Ancient Locations) are the point of the whole of Hegra/Mada'in Salih, and the brief bars a region or namesake point for a single chamber. The Madain Project article is built with scripts and returns no readable text, so the stored point stays for the owner.

The Catalan article dates the site only by period words, 'des d'inicis de l'època talaiòtica ( bronze final ) fins al talaiòtic final', and its one absolute date, about 500 BC, is explicitly attributed to excavations at other settlements while stating that of this site no data are known, so nothing dates the start of Torrellisar and the field stays empty.

No source dates the start of Usqunta (Lucanas, Ayacucho). The English article and the heritage declaration of 2009/2011 give only its name, location and mountain height - a period word alone would not count, and none is even given here.

English and Spanish Wikipedia name Choquequirao Puquio (San Sebastian, Cusco; not the Vilcabamba Choquequirao) only as an archaeological site, the infobox giving the Inca culture as a period word; no source gives a year, century or millennium for its start.

No source gives a point for the Osztrópataka burial itself. The English Wikipedia article on the treasure carries no coordinates, and the Wikidata item Q18167176 has no coordinate statement, only a discovery year and the two museums that keep the finds. The village of Ostrovany is not the burial, so its coordinates cannot be used for the site.

The Wikidata item Q15950097 for Wanakawri, Huanuco carries no coordinate (P625) statement, and no article or register page I could read gives a point for it. The Britannica and travel pages linked from the site's own page are about the city of Huanuco, not this site. With no quotable point the stored point stays as it is.

No source dates the start of Wanakawri, Huanuco. The Wikidata item Q15950097 has no inception (P571) statement and no article describes the site, so nothing gives a year, century or millennium for its construction. The field stays empty.

English Wikipedia says the Way was in use 'at least as early as the Iron Age' and that its prehistoric origin has been questioned, with first documentary mentions in Anglo-Saxon charters from 903; these give period words and a first mention, not a dated start. The North Herts Museum page cited is not available (404).

Wikipedia and the MINCETUR inventory date Qollmay only to the Inca Empire / Late Horizon Inca (a period word); the only 15th-century date is on a content-farm page, which is not usable. No year, century or millennium from a reputable source.

No readable page prints a point for the ancient theatre of Fethiye itself; the only coordinates on the Telmessos article (36°36′59″K 29°6′41″D) belong to the Telmessos archaeological site as a whole, which is the city rather than the theatre, so they cannot stand for this site.

Livius dates the theater only to "this age", the age of the Seleucid and Pergamene empires, without a year, century or millennium of its own, and the Telmessos article reports only that the theatre remains came to light in excavations; no source gives a year, century or millennium for the construction or first use of this theatre.

No source gives a point for Waqlamarka (Hacjlasmarca). The mincetur ficha 3723 for Zona Arqueologica de Huaclas Marca de Parco, the national record the Wikipedia article cites, prints no coordinates - only department, province, district and altitude - and the article's infobox carries {{coord missing}}. The stored point stays as it is.

Neither the English Wikipedia article (its infobox has an empty coordinates field) nor the Wikidata item Q15950015 carries a coordinate statement, and the Peruvian tourism inventory record cited by the article is no longer readable at its MINCETUR address, so no source can be quoted for the site's point.

The English Wikipedia article says only that the site is an archaeological site in the Carapo District and was declared National Cultural Heritage; it gives no year, century or millennium for its start.
No readable page prints a point for Los Sapos in a form the check reads; only an OpenStreetMap-derived aggregator gives a point with extra text around the numbers.
No source found dates Awkimarka in Apurímac (Pomacocha / Tumay Huaraca); Wikipedia gives no date and the Chanka literature speaks of the Late Intermediate Period only for the region as a whole.

No readable page found prints a point for Selva di Malano; the Soriano nel Cimino ArteCitta page and Italian Wikipedia name the place without coordinates (OpenStreetMap places the wood near the stored point, but that is not a quotable page).
The ArteCitta page gives only the period word 'Etruscan Roman period' for the villages, necropolis and rock monuments; no year or century dates the start.
MINCETUR's record says only that the prehispanic settlement dates to the Late Intermediate Period (intermedio tardio), a period word with no year or century; no source dates the start.

The only source with a year is the Spanish Wikipedia infobox (construction 600-900 AD), which contradicts its own text (abandoned in the 8th century) and the scholarly abstract (Escobedo 1997: founded in the Early Classic); English Wikipedia says only the middle half of the Classic period; no source gives a reliable start year for the site.

Neither the English Taliata article (which carries Wikipedia's 'missing geocoordinate data' marker) nor the Wikidata item Q61129061 states any coordinate for the site, so no source point can be quoted and the stored point stays.

No readable page prints a point for the Treasury of the Acanthians itself: Wikidata Q22810172 has no coordinate, no Wikipedia article (en, el, it) prints one and Commons has no category for it; only the sanctuary of Delphi as a whole has points, which are not the treasury's own.

The sources call the building a treasury in the sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi; no readable source names it a temple, monument or sanctuary itself, and no canonical type means treasury, so no type can be quoted without stretching a source.
